items.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I discovered Earl Garner, right. ... He just helped me. All the beauty and lyricism is right there.

ctx.x: Was this always your desire? Well, at four . . .

I don‘t know. I didn‘t know what I wanted, you see. I just know I wanted the music. It wasn‘t like, well, what direction? I just wanted to play the piano. But I had classical training in the beginning, and that‘s what I knew, you know. And I wanted to. I wanted to, to be a classical artist, but I don‘t know, something happened with it. Earl Garner [phonetic] came along and he kind of said, ―Ooh, ooh, ooh,‖ you know.
With Penthouse Serenade? Was that one of the many?
